docs.title: Dense classifier: MNIST digits
docs.text: Dataset: MNIST as JPG Architecture: 784 → 128 → 64 → 10 Task: Image classification

docs.title: Why this architecture?
docs.text: The example flattens a 28×28 grayscale image to 784 features before two dense ReLU layers and a softmax output.

docs.title: Training and evaluation
docs.text:
Only two images per digit are sampled for a quick functional check. Low accuracy is expected; it is not a benchmark of a fully trained classifier.

Run the complete program from the repository root:

python src/Kafe.py docs/ejemplos/gesha-nivel-8-mnist.kf

-- Dense classifier: MNIST digits: image classification with MNIST as JPG.
import kaggle;
import machine;
import gesha;

MACHINE dataset = kaggle.load_image_folder_dataset("scolianni/mnistasjpg", 28, 28, "gray", 0, "trainingSample");
List[List[List[List[FLOAT]]]] images = dataset[0];
List[INT] labels = dataset[1];
List[List[FLOAT]] X = [];
List[INT] y = [];
for (digit in range(0, 10)):
    INT selected = 0;
    INT i = 0;
    while (i < len(labels)):
        if (labels[i] == digit):
            if (selected < 2):
                List[FLOAT] pixels = [];
                for (row in range(0, 28)):
                    for (column in range(0, 28)):
                        append(pixels, images[i][0][row][column]);
                    ;
                ;
                append(X, pixels);
                append(y, digit);
                selected = selected + 1;
            ;
        ;
        i = i + 1;
    ;
;
show("Selected labeled images:");
show(len(X));
MACHINE split = machine.stratified_train_test_split(X, y, 0.5, 42);
List[List[FLOAT]] X_train = split[0];
List[List[FLOAT]] X_test = split[1];
List[INT] y_train = split[2];
List[INT] y_test = split[3];

GESHA h1 = gesha.create_dense(128, "relu", [784], 0.0, 42, gesha.he_normal(42));
GESHA h2 = gesha.create_dense(64, "relu", [128], 0.0, 43, gesha.he_normal(43));
GESHA output_layer = gesha.create_dense(10, "softmax", [64], 0.0, 44, gesha.glorot_uniform(44));
GESHA model = gesha.sequential([h1, h2, output_layer]);
model.compile("adam", "sparse_categorical_crossentropy", []);
model.set_lr(0.01);
model.fit(X_train, y_train, 4, 2);

List[INT] predictions = model.predict_label(X_test);
INT correct = 0;
for (i in range(0, len(y_test))):
    if (predictions[i] == y_test[i]):
        correct = correct + 1;
    ;
    show("Digit actual=" + str(y_test[i]) + " predicted=" + str(predictions[i]));
;
show("MNIST test accuracy (small teaching sample):");
show(correct / len(y_test));

docs.title: Regression MLP: Red Wine Quality
docs.text: Dataset: Red Wine Quality Architecture: 11 → 32 → 16 → 1 Task: Multivariable regression

docs.title: Why this architecture?
docs.text: Eleven physicochemical measurements feed a ReLU network with a linear output.

docs.title: Training and evaluation
docs.text:
Fit the scaler on training data and report test MAE after converting predictions back to quality points.

Run the complete program from the repository root:

python src/Kafe.py docs/ejemplos/gesha-nivel-7-wine.kf

-- Regression MLP: Red Wine Quality: multivariable regression with Red Wine Quality.
import kaggle;
import machine;
import gesha;

List[STR] columns = [
    "fixed acidity", "volatile acidity", "citric acid", "residual sugar", "chlorides",
    "free sulfur dioxide", "total sulfur dioxide", "density", "pH", "sulphates", "alcohol"
];
List[List[FLOAT]] X = kaggle.load_dataset_matrix("uciml/red-wine-quality-cortez-et-al-2009", columns, "winequality-red.csv", 240);
PARDOS df = kaggle.load_dataset("uciml/red-wine-quality-cortez-et-al-2009", "winequality-red.csv");
List[INT] quality = df.col("quality");
List[FLOAT] y = [];
for (i in range(0, len(X))):
    append(y, (float(quality[i]) - 3.0) / 5.0);
;
MACHINE split = machine.train_test_split(X, y, 0.2, 42);
List[List[FLOAT]] X_train = split[0];
List[List[FLOAT]] X_test = split[1];
List[FLOAT] y_train = split[2];
List[FLOAT] y_test = split[3];
MACHINE scaler = machine.standard_scaler();
scaler.fit(X_train);
List[List[FLOAT]] train_scaled = scaler.transform(X_train);
List[List[FLOAT]] test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test);

GESHA h1 = gesha.create_dense(32, "relu", [11], 0.0, 42, gesha.he_normal(42));
GESHA h2 = gesha.create_dense(16, "relu", [32], 0.0, 43, gesha.he_normal(43));
GESHA output_layer = gesha.create_dense(1, "linear", [16], 0.0, 44);
GESHA model = gesha.sequential([h1, h2, output_layer]);
model.compile("adam", "mse", []);
model.set_lr(0.005);
model.fit(train_scaled, y_train, 30, 16);

FLOAT error = 0.0;
for (i in range(0, len(y_test))):
    FLOAT pred = model.predict(test_scaled[i])[0] * 5.0 + 3.0;
    FLOAT actual = y_test[i] * 5.0 + 3.0;
    FLOAT difference = pred - actual;
    if (difference < 0.0):
        difference = 0.0 - difference;
    ;
    error = error + difference;
    if (i < 5):
        show("Wine actual=" + str(actual) + " predicted=" + str(pred));
    ;
;
show("Red Wine MAE test en puntos de quality:");
show(error / len(y_test));

docs.title: Interpreting the results
docs.text:
For supervised models, split the data before fitting a scaler to avoid data leakage. Classification accuracy measures the fraction of correct labels. Regression uses mean absolute error (MAE) and R² on the test set. The reported values are from one seeded educational run, not cross-validation.

Clustering has no ground-truth target in these examples. Cluster IDs are arbitrary and do not correspond to class labels. The silhouette score compares within-cluster cohesion with separation when more than one cluster is present. Spatial plots help inspect the assignments, but they do not replace metrics.

docs.title: Error types
docs.text: KAFE handles errors at different stages of execution. When possible, each error includes a type, a descriptive message, and a location.

docs.title: Error categories
docs.text: Category Phase Example SyntaxError Lexical/syntactic analysis Unrecognized token or invalid structure TypeError Execution (semantic) Incorrect data type NameError Execution (semantic) Undefined variable or function IndexError Execution (runtime) Index out of range RuntimeError Execution (runtime) Infinite loop or general runtime error FileNotFoundError Execution (runtime) File or module not found FileExistsError Execution (runtime) File already exists

docs.title: Handling strategy
docs.text:
KAFE distinguishes between:

  • .error.kf files: Expected test errors → exit code 1, stderr
  • Regular programs: Unexpected errors → stdout, exit code 0
# In Kafe.py
try:
    main()
except Exception as e:
    if sys.argv[1].endswith(".error.kf"):
        print(error_msg, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print(error_msg)
        sys.exit(0)

docs.title: Implemented and approved behavior
docs.text:
The Tutor is one conversation. Enter or Send submits once; Shift+Enter adds a newline; IME composition cannot submit. One assistant answer streams into one message. Stop replaces Send while responding, and the next draft remains editable. Retry uses the original question and current authorized context without duplicating the learner message or automatically resending after key configuration.

The Prepare/Review/Send request pipeline, provenance/payload cards, readiness messages and formal goal/milestone/check/progress workflow were removed from production. Teaching, plans and summaries remain ordinary dialogue. Existing legacy progress is preserved and omitted from provider context. Its separately confirmed clear command does not reset chat or credentials.

The eligible active .kf is included by default. Other visible same-workspace .kf files are metadata only until explicitly selected. An optional selection survives becoming active, returning to another editor and closing its own editors. Active source capture happens once. Explicit removal, lost authorization, Restricted Mode and New conversation revoke selection.

Conversation, draft, selection, requests and output are host-memory state. View recreation retains the live state; host restart discards it. New conversation preserves credentials, legacy records and an independently running process.

Restricted Mode has production manifest support limited: message-only conversation is available, while workspace files, file tools, edits and Run require trust. The production manifest is the native fixture's capability source; development-host activation does not substitute for installed acceptance.

Send only stages a proposed change. Review change opens the native diff; Apply requires reviewed identity and matching target/dependency authorization, URI, version and hash. Dismiss discards it. Authorized editor-focus changes do not discard a settled proposal, but edits/deletion of any captured dependency, trust loss and reset revoke it. Applying does not Run.

Run remains explicit, saved-file and named-target bound. Its process/PTY owner survives chat reset and closes once when the process settles. Provider tools cannot execute programs. Settled exitCode: null renders an unknown exit outcome and bounded partial stdout/stderr/truncation; missing exitCode remains unsettled.

Validated cached knowledge is independent of executable runtime readiness. An unavailable pack produces an honest limitation; integrity/lineage changes fail closed. Initial retrieval uses a separate trimmed first-300-character query while preserving the full submitted message. Tool retrieval retains its original bounds. Continued tool rounds use the already authorized pack without a second Send.

Retained bounds: eight eligible whole history pairs within 32 KiB UTF-8, 64 KiB per source snapshot, 1 MiB Run evidence, four tools, four calls per round and four rounds per turn. Source revision fencing covers awaited capture and immediate provider admission. Secrets, source bytes, requests, transcripts and raw transport errors are not persisted or logged by the Tutor.

See PRODUCT.md, extension README and extension guide. The 2026-10-04 approved design now uses Kilo as visual and interaction authority, without copying its framework/assets/services. Reference repository: https://github.com/kilo-org/kilocode, inspected revision ccb6673bf501b1d64ed3711e97d8572128298fa7. The sibling clone is outside this repository and is not pushed here.

docs.title: Alignment with the Kafe DevKit evaluation proposal
docs.text:
This document maps the supplied evaluation proposal to Tutor behavior and evidence that a human evaluator can review. It is a study preparation guide, not evidence of educational effectiveness. The proposal describes two university groups, approximately 40–60 available participants, and a minimum of 84 minutes: a 12-minute pretest, two 30-minute practical activities and a 12-minute posttest. Instructions, informed consent and the usability/perception instruments require additional time.

The current intended pretest and posttest each have six short-answer questions: three ML and three DL, scored 0–2 each, maximum 12. The user confirmed this version against the revised proposal's six-row content table, 12-point rubric and supplied form fragments; the proposal's remaining eight-question wording is stale. Earlier repository descriptions of eight one-point items are superseded. The eight conceptual topics below remain broader teaching coverage, not questionnaire items.

This alignment uses the supplied proposal's main document text, form HTML fragments, SUS/upload screenshots and architecture diagram. The originals remain unchanged. DOCX text was extracted, but rendering was unavailable; no page/layout verification is claimed. No live form or image endpoint was visited or submitted. Three questions per form reference images whose data were not supplied; their contents and equivalent difficulty remain unknown. The fragments say to select “No sé” while offering short-text controls without that selectable option. The research team must reconcile instructions, accessibility, missing image data, version pairing and scoring reliability before administration. No item text or answer key is bundled into production guidance.

docs.title: Conceptual traceability
docs.text:
Objective from the proposal Appropriate Tutor support during practical work Observable evidence and interpretation limits ML 1. Sensitivity Explain sensitivity/recall as the fraction of actual positive cases detected, TP / (TP + FN). Establish which label denotes fraud and connect missed fraud to false negatives. Interpret available observed or learner-reported values. Learner explains a confusion matrix or recall calculation and its relevance to fraud. A numerical metric alone does not show that the learner understands it. ML 2. Comparing classifiers Help compare the supplied starter classifier, logistic regression and Gaussian Naive Bayes on the same held-out cases. Explain competing criteria and invite a justified choice. The .kf program, comparable results and the learner's conclusion identify the comparison and rationale. The Tutor must not choose the final submitted answer for the learner. ML 3. Imbalanced data Explain why predicting the majority class can produce high accuracy while missing fraud. Discuss class counts, recall, precision and the consequences of false positives and false negatives. Learner relates class imbalance to the reported metrics. An accuracy-only ranking is insufficient evidence of minority-class detection. API options must follow the reviewed MACHINE contracts. ML 4. Evaluation with new data Explain training versus held-out evaluation and why repeated use of the training cases does not establish generalization. Keep preprocessing fitted on training data when explaining a valid evaluation workflow. Distinct training/evaluation data and the learner's explanation support the observation. A successful run or a high training score cannot establish performance on unseen transactions. DL 1. Interpreting predictions Connect the four XOR inputs to their expected labels, then help interpret the model's actual outputs, shapes and documented output activation. Distinguish a numeric prediction from the rule used to assign a class. Learner compares predictions with XOR targets and explains discrepancies. The Tutor must not invent predictions or infer success from code that has not been run. DL 2. Representation capacity Explain why one linear decision boundary cannot separate XOR and why hidden layers require nonlinear transformations to change that capacity. Invite the learner's architectural reasoning. The learner's diagram, explanation or controlled architecture experiment supports interpretation. More layers alone do not guarantee successful training. DL 3. Learning rate Explain the effect of update size, unstable training and slow convergence. Support a controlled experiment that distinguishes learning rate, epochs, architecture and initialization. Recorded settings and observed runs support a comparison. A different seed or more epochs cannot by itself repair the representational limit of a single linear separator. DL 4. Overfitting Explain fitting observed cases versus generalization, and the limits of conclusions from training loss alone. Learner identifies what additional held-out evidence would be needed. The four XOR truth-table cases describe the complete stated Boolean task; fitting those cases alone does not estimate generalization to a separate population or demonstrate overfitting. The evaluator must define any additional evaluation data and claim.

Reviewed positional APIs, input shapes and implementation limits are documented in the MACHINE contracts and GESHA API coverage. References support explanations; repository examples and their expected outputs are not observations of a participant's program.

KAFE metric distinction: machine.recall_score computes macro recall over the classes present in the reference labels. It does not automatically report sensitivity for the fraud-positive class, and there is no average= option in the current positional DSL API. Establish the positive label and the confusion-matrix class order before interpreting TP and FN. For a chosen class with no actual positive cases, TP / (TP + FN) is undefined; distinguish that mathematical limit from the API's documented zero-denominator convention.

docs.title: Practical activities and learner participation
docs.text:
For the fraud activity, the learner executes and interprets the supplied starter classifier, explores logistic regression and Gaussian Naive Bayes, compares all three and writes an individual conclusion. The Tutor should explain unfamiliar concepts and available KAFE calls, provide bounded hints or illustrative fragments, and respond to the learner's own reasoning. It may calculate and organize supplied evidence directly while leaving the final assessed comparison and conclusion to the learner. It must not replace the activity with a ready-to-submit program or a final model choice. The proposal does not identify the starter classifier by name and includes no starter program or dataset. The separately attributed facilitator package below supplies new starting materials; its shallow tree is not the proposal's original unnamed model.

For the XOR activity, the learner begins with one neuron, examines the results and considers the proposal's three alternatives: more epochs, a different learning rate or added layers. Initialization seed is an additional controlled-training condition, not a fourth alternative listed in the proposal. The Tutor should clarify the distinction between representational capacity and training behavior while leaving the proposed experiment and justification to the learner. An affine threshold cannot represent XOR; composing only affine layers remains affine, while nonlinear hidden transformations change capacity without guaranteeing convergence. It may help diagnose the learner's implementation without supplying the complete exercise solution. Stochastic training outcomes must be described as observations of particular settings, not promised results.

Meaningful participation can be sought in questions, proposed alternatives, decisions, changed settings, comparisons, checks and individual explanations. A checkpoint confirmation records adoption of a displayed choice; a Tutor-written summary is an unconfirmed interpretation. Neither is independent evidence of learner reasoning or mastery. Explanations, sketches, pseudocode and concise technical answers can all be relevant evidence; the final research rubric must specify how evaluators judge them.

One guided Tutor offers direct concept explanations and focused reasoning at meaningful choices. Requests for shorter or fuller explanations affect presentation within eligible bounded conversation history; they create no durable style memory or inferred ability. Paused teaching removes additional reasoning requirements; it does not authorize writing files, executing a program or supplying a complete assessment answer. Direct concept questions deserve a useful explanation rather than an obligatory quiz. The Tutor should reuse already supplied answers and metrics instead of repeatedly asking for them.

The engineering target now includes first-semester learners, whereas the proposal describes second- and third-semester groups. Readiness guidance should use familiar language, explain before asking, offer one manageable next step and correct the learner's actual misconception. A short explanation, sketch or draft can already supply useful reasoning; feedback should affirm supported claims and identify an actual gap only if present. This target does not establish that either activity can be completed by novices within its 30-minute allocation. Executable starting materials are prepared; first-use orientation, classroom runtime/provider setup and a facilitated novice pilot remain prerequisites for a classroom readiness claim.

docs.title: Facilitator classroom materials
docs.text:
A separate local deliverable, kafe-classroom-starters.zip, contains seven files: Spanish instructions, DATA-NOTICE.md, provenance.json, separate training/evaluation CSVs, fraud-baseline.kf and xor-one-neuron.kf. The independently reviewed archive is 490,107 bytes, SHA256 96819195821a0dbf829a85138349badf3a962f980619daaedb3a85893ff03e9d. It is a facilitator handoff, with no public download URL or bundled interpreter. It contains one shallow-tree implementation and the one-neuron XOR starting point; the other classifier implementations, final network and individual conclusions remain learner work. Teacher programs/results and original source-row IDs stay outside the learner archive.

The historical anonymized ULB/Worldline credit-card source comes through OpenML dataset 1597, with original publisher attribution and ODbL 1.0 database / DbCL 1.0 contents notices retained. A full chronological 80/20 source split precedes fixed seed-42 sampling. The resulting 1,600 training and 400 evaluation rows contain 80 and 20 frauds respectively: a disclosed 5% didactic enrichment, rather than the source prevalence or current banking conditions. Predictors are V1–V28 and Amount; Class, Time and row identifiers are excluded. Scaling is learned from training only. No selected predictor vector crosses partitions; repeated vectors remain within training. Upstream PCA cannot be refitted or audited from the available source, and 20 evaluation frauds limit sensitivity resolution to five percentage points per case. The data notice records these limitations and redistribution terms separately from KAFE's software license.

Retained actual teacher CLI outputs were independently checked beyond exit status, including every predicted fraud label, matrix axes, counts and empty diagnostic streams. The baseline works from the repository and extracted-kit working directories. The three particular fraud runs and one-neuron/nonlinear XOR checks establish executable feasibility with fixed inputs and settings; they do not choose a learner's model or guarantee convergence, generalization, lesson timing or educational effectiveness. The archive is not an extension installation, runtime deployment or research-data upload. Facilitators must prepare the intended machines and preserve the complete extracted folder before a supervised novice pilot.

docs.title: Honest execution evidence
docs.text:
A learner-started Run can provide private, bounded stdout, stderr, an exit outcome, truncation information and runtime/source observations. For the currently authorized active file, the composer includes that observation in the provider snapshot and getLatestRunResult reads the captured result. A metadata label such as “not a correctness check” does not mean that output is absent. The Tutor can interpret available metric values without reproducing the raw output block as its response.

If the learner supplies numbers in a message, the Tutor may explain and compare them as learner-reported values. This does not authorize a claim that the extension observed a Run. If relevant metrics are absent, it should explain what can already be inferred and ask only for the indispensable missing values. Missing output does not justify inventing results, repeatedly requesting values already present, or refusing all conceptual help.

Runs from another active file do not supply raw output for the current file. When the same file has changed, earlier output can remain available with explicit historical/changed-source labels; it does not verify the edited code. The host separately observes saved-file boundaries and the current editor contents, and does not claim exact executed bytes. New, switched and restored conversations clear private Run evidence and executable permissions. The combined private stdout/stderr bound remains 1 MiB, and restricted workspaces do not authorize file or Run tools.

An observed exit code is not a correctness verdict. A passing example, a learner explanation, a confirmation click or a Tutor response cannot establish mastery, learning gains or the causal efficacy of Kafe DevKit. Automated regression tests check context transport, provenance, bounds and instructions; they do not establish that every live provider response follows the pedagogy.

Development-only activity-dialogues.json supplies two three-turn Spanish rehearsals with synthetic observations, internal mathematical oracles and actual-answer review criteria. Production coordinator/composer tests submit only exact learner text and retain eligible whole pairs; rubrics stay offline. Canned replies verify transport and authority boundaries only. Three six-turn Flash/Pro samples were rejected, the guided-7 six-plus-two round was mixed, and the final seven-reply 9c25d04 sample was not accepted: fraud comparison and bounded constructor help coexist with material XOR baseline, evidence-origin, isolation and draft-feedback failures. The user chose to keep this checkpoint on 2026-10-28 and stop further model/reasoning experiments. The full answer-quality goal remains incomplete; Pro is an experimental comparison default without a winner or student-readiness claim. The 33 tuning requests and earlier separate four-message pilot establish no novice comprehension, lesson completion or learning result. Source 9c25d04 passed exact-revision real VS Code 1.96 trusted/untrusted CI and packaging; that engineering gate is separate from empirical novice efficacy and final documentation-checkpoint delivery. See Tutor reliability for exact rounds, limitations and receipts.

docs.title: Collection, export and consent
docs.text:
The proposal asks for the participant's .kf program, execution results when available, an individual conclusion and Tutor interactions when there is interaction and authorization to analyze it. Keep these as distinguishable evidence sources. Execution results may require a separately authorized collection method because private host Run evidence is deliberately absent from saved/exported transcripts.

Each workspace can retain independent local conversations. The learner explicitly selects a conversation and exports it as versioned UTF-8 JSON through a native Save dialog. Export contains visible messages, statuses and safe summaries, including text or code the learner typed. It excludes the unsent draft, preferences, provider history/dependencies, attached source snapshots, private Run evidence, credentials and executable handles. A visible learner message that quotes results or includes identifying text remains part of the export; export does not promise automatic anonymization.

Saving a local conversation or opening the export dialog is not research consent. The research team must obtain informed consent, define which artifacts may be analyzed, establish participant identifiers and handling/retention rules, and review shared copies for identifying information. The extension does not automatically upload transcripts to a research repository, generate participation scores or supply an efficacy dashboard. Provider requests made during assistance are separate from any research collection; participants must receive the applicable information before participating. See the extension guide for context and conversation controls.

docs.title: Independent measurement and human procedures
docs.text:
The proposal requires individual pretest and posttest responses without documentation, Internet or AI assistance. KAFE Tutor should be unavailable for those sessions through facilitator procedure; the extension has no proctoring mode that enforces questionnaire conditions. Practical activities allow Kafe DevKit, official documentation and KAFE Tutor, while the proposal excludes external AI assistants. The facilitator owns that distinction and its communication.

Research item Status represented by the proposal Work still owned by the research team Six-item conceptual pretest and posttest Six short-answer items per form, three ML and three DL; human rubric 0–2 each, maximum 12. Resolve the remaining source/form mismatches, missing images and accessibility; review keys, coverage, equivalent difficulty, scoring consistency, individual pairing and independent administration. Analyze actual collected scores. Practical performance rubric Construction, execution, interpretation, checking and justification are proposed. Finalize observable anchors and evaluator procedure; pilot before claiming comparable scores. Adapted ICAP observation Passive, Active, Constructive, Interactive and Not evaluable categories; three evidence sources and descriptive/exploratory analysis are specified. Human evaluators apply the procedure below, document classification decisions and assess agreement. No empirical validity or reliability result is supplied. Tutor accompaniment Pedagogical accompaniment remains an intended dimension. A completed dedicated accompaniment rubric is not established by its mention; define/review criteria and human judgment procedure. System Usability Scale (SUS) Ten ordered statements, five response options and the standard contribution calculation are specified; administration follows both practical activities. Preserve instrument order and authorized language/version; apply the procedure below to actual responses. Language-version validation and participant scores are not established. Perceived experience An intended additional dimension. Finalize its separate instrument, procedure and analysis; do not infer satisfaction from continued use.

docs.title: Adapted ICAP observation
docs.text:
At the end of both activities, the proposal combines three sources: the individual's brief decision record (strategies, tests and justifications), developed .kf solutions with execution results, and authorized Tutor interactions. Human review produces a profile per learner and activity, identifying observable behaviors:

Category Operational interpretation Passive Receives information or observes results without observable manipulation or elaboration. Active Executes, applies or manipulates supplied information without new explanation or inference. Constructive Generates an explanation, hypothesis, inference or justified decision beyond the supplied information. Interactive Substantive reciprocal exchange develops, questions or revises ideas; the learner contributes reasoning. Not evaluable Evidence is insufficient to classify the process, even if a final artifact exists.

Message counts, a Run, a confirmation or Tutor-written summaries do not determine classification. Interactive participation requires evidence of reciprocal construction. Report category distributions and descriptive ML/DL comparisons; relationships with practical performance and pre/post changes are exploratory. The adapted rubric alone cannot demonstrate deep understanding or general autonomy. No automatic ICAP score/classification is implemented, and inter-rater agreement remains to be established.

docs.title: SUS administration and interpretation
docs.text:
The supplied procedure administers ten ordered statements through Google Forms after both practical activities, evaluating the complete experienced environment: VS Code, KAFE and KAFE Tutor. Preserve the ten items, their order and five options coded 1–5. Human analysis uses response minus 1 for odd-numbered items and 5 minus response for even-numbered items; sum the contributions and multiply by 2.5 for a 0–100 score. This is a scale score, not a percentage of correct answers. The extension does not administer or automatically score it.

Report valid questionnaire count, mean and standard deviation, median and interquartile range, distributions and academic-group summaries where group size permits. No actual responses or SUS result are supplied. After a brief experience SUS describes perceived usability; it does not establish timing efficiency, accessibility, absence of technical errors or pedagogical effectiveness. Interpret it alongside practical and participation evidence. Voluntary participation, email registration and a later transcript upload each require the research team's distinct information/consent procedure; none follows from local storage or export.

For real paired questionnaire data, the proposal defines individual change as posttest score minus pretest score and proposes descriptive summaries, ML/DL differences and item-level analysis. The suitability of a paired statistical analysis and an effect estimate remains a research decision based on the collected data and study design. No participant data, empirical learning effect, usability score or efficacy conclusion is supplied by this alignment document.

docs.text:

The extension version is 0.0.8. Its reviewed fixture catalogue uses the renamed English test directories, and its bundled references have been regenerated. Local .kf programs and obsolete bin/ interpreter builds are excluded from the VSIX. Existing untracked learner files are preserved.

docs.title: Publication order
docs.text:
1. Build the runtime ZIP and sidecar from the pinned Git revision with scripts/build-runtime-release.py.
  2. Publish both files under the matching GitHub release tag.
  3. Verify the uploaded asset names, target revision, and GitHub SHA-256 digest.
  4. Set releasePublished to true in src/runtimeManifest.json.
  5. Build and inspect the VSIX with vsce package.
  6. Install the VSIX locally with code --install-extension <file> --force and run a .kf file.
  7. Publish that same verified VSIX to Visual Studio Marketplace.

This order matters because KAFE: Install Runtime refuses unpublished pinned assets. A VSIX published before its runtime release would install successfully but could not prepare KAFE for execution.

docs.title: Maintaining KAFE Tutor code guidance
docs.text:
Extension 2.3.0 bundles KAFE fundamentals, reviewed MACHINE/GESHA API contracts, canonical library documentation, tutorial text and selected complete repository fixtures. English and Spanish requests use the same version-matched sources. The references and bundled knowledge tool lookup work before executable runtime or managed-pack setup, including message-only Restricted Mode. A bare greeting receives fundamentals without incidental library/example search; the teaching policy keeps it brief.

The intended top-level inventory contains 58 MACHINE functions, 56 GESHA wrappers and five activation aliases. Reviewed receiver contracts also describe methods, properties, argument/shape constraints and supported, limited, experimental, deprecated or unsupported behavior. These are 512 reference records: 420 MACHINE and 92 GESHA, rather than 512 independent learner capabilities. All 58 MACHINE functions, 55 usable GESHA wrappers and five activation aliases have successful direct KAFE evidence. The remaining GESHA wrapper, l1_l2_regularizer, has negative evidence for its unavailable GESHA binding. Backend-only hooks and known limits are documented without changing the runtime.

Curated reference/machine-api.json and reference/gesha-api.json feed generated src/tutor/libraryReferences.json. Contracts use actual positional KAFE call forms, return types and reviewed evidence. Source-derived inventory and receiver-member checks reject missing records. An explicit reviewed source fingerprint and runtime revision require renewed review when semantics change; ordinary regeneration cannot advance that attestation. Contract, corpus, evidence and content hashes detect drift. The current and actual pinned interpreter fingerprints must match. The pinned revision must exist locally; CI fetches full history. A checkout-only test does not establish pinned-runtime compatibility.

The shared reference/knowledge-corpus.json selects canonical documentation/grammar and Markdown/KAFE tutorials from docs/ejemplos, mapped to examples/tutorials. SVGs are excluded explicitly. Bundled generation, development packs and future managed builds use this selection; safe paths, exact identities and 512-file / 256 KiB-per-file / 8 MiB-total limits remain. The published runtime 0.3.0 assets stay unchanged. Updated managed packs require a future committed source revision and versioned release; historical revisions without a corpus manifest retain the six required legacy sections. Current bundled MACHINE/GESHA contracts and tutorials take precedence over old managed library narratives.

Exact qualified names, reviewed API aliases and normalized case, accents, camelCase and underscores support bilingual retrieval. Fundamentals remain separate. Library selection admits at most three complete units and 8 KiB; library material and fixtures together share 12 KiB. Each admitted library/example unit is at most 6 KiB. Bundled tool lookup admits at most five units and 12 KiB. Managed/development search retains five passages, two per file and 2,000 characters per passage. Headings, signatures, tables, fences and standalone source units remain intact; oversized or incomplete fenced units are omitted instead of clipped into runnable-looking code. Generated omission records retain those limits. Full library coverage does not require sending the entire corpus on every request.

src/tutor/kafeReferences.json contains reviewed .kf, .expec and optional .in pairs from reference/catalogue.json, including labelled expected-error fixtures. Unreviewed fixtures remain listed as omitted; missing expectations fail generation. Fixture examples retain complete code/input/expected results, at most three examples within the remaining shared reference budget. Licensing is preserved in packaged references. Bundled provenance never impersonates a ready managed/development pack, a learner file or a host-observed execution. Matching reference identities do not prove an installed runtime, a new program or a model answer correct.

docs.title: Contributor workflow
docs.text:
Use Node 24 LTS. Install extension dependencies inside kafe-vscode before launching the Development Host:

npm ci
npm audit --audit-level=low

For each language or library change:

  1. Review actual pinned wrapper argument checks, returned objects and supported DSL behavior. Update the relevant API JSON, source-symbol mappings, documentation, aliases and valid/negative KAFE evidence. Keep unsupported paths explicit; incidental Python imports and default arguments are not public DSL APIs. If source identity changes, coordinate the runtime/version pin and renew the curated review attestation after review rather than editing hashes to bypass a failure.
  2. Keep pure deterministic teaching examples in reference/catalogue.json. Declare filesystem examples and their reviewed local assets separately in the API file's isolatedFixtures; the weights workflow is isolated evidence, not a pure teaching fixture. Long training, network downloads and credentials require separately identified integration checks. Do not execute generated model code for reference verification.
  3. Update reference/essentials.md only for core syntax/execution changes. Add documentation/tutorial inputs through the shared corpus manifest; presentation assets do not enter reference text.
  4. Run npm run references:build, npm run references:check and npm run test:unit from kafe-vscode. These commands cover fundamentals/fixtures and library contracts/corpus/evidence. Freshness, completeness, bilingual retrieval, unavailable APIs, intact-unit budgets and packaging are distinct checks. Cross-language corpus tests need Python; KAFE_PYTHON can select an installed interpreter.
  5. Prepare Python 3.11+ and ANTLR 4.13.2. Archive src/ from runtimeManifest.json's pinned sourceRevision into an ignored directory and generate its parser there. Set KAFE_REFERENCE_RUNTIME_ROOT to that directory. From the repository root run uv run --locked --group dev python kafe-vscode/scripts/verify-tutor-references.py and uv run --locked --group dev python kafe-vscode/scripts/verify-library-references.py. Each verifier checks the actual pinned source; reviewed fixtures run in disposable copies, with declared local assets staged for isolated cases. Use uv run --locked --group dev pytest tests/ -q for broader checkout regression evidence.
  6. Package locally and inspect the VSIX. It must contain generated library/reference data, their loaders, the shared corpus/search helpers, corpus definition and fixture license. Runtime assets remain separately published. Packaging, installing, publishing and observing hosted CI require their own evidence.

Run native/package checks from kafe-vscode using existing installed tools:

node test/run-extension-host-tests.js
node --test test/native/host-policy.test.cjs
node test/native/acceptance.cjs <absolute-ignored-evidence-directory>
node node_modules/@vscode/vsce/vsce package --out <absolute-ignored-output.vsix>
node test/verify-vsix.js <same-absolute-output.vsix>

Native checks require the exact cached VS Code 1.96.0 host and isolated trusted/restricted profiles. They do not download it locally. Provisioning is restricted to genuine GitHub CI; do not spoof that environment, bypass provisioning or substitute the installed regular editor. If the cache is absent, record local native checks as unavailable; use a completed exact-revision hosted receipt when one exists, or the existing hosted workflow after separate push/dispatch authorization. Package inspection does not authorize installation or publication. npm ci has the documented upstream Mocha/glob deprecation exception; audits remain complete and blocking, with the unused signing-helper install script denied.

Reference verification requires full token consumption without parser/lexer diagnostics, warnings treated as errors, exact exit codes and both complete output streams. This catches the parser's ability to stop before an unexpected trailing else. Controlled fundamentals also exercise input, conditional chains, built-in output, user-defined print and explicit invocation. Library verification joins successful token-observed top-level calls to the intended inventory, with unavailable paths retaining negative evidence. Zero exit alone is never a passing check. Parsing and execution each have a 15-second timeout. Disposable copies avoid mutating the checkout; they are not a security sandbox for arbitrary code. Run only reviewed repository fixtures in this development/CI gate, never silently in a learner project.

The extension workflow watches extension, interpreter, test, documentation and lock/configuration inputs. It checks freshness and API evidence against the pinned interpreter, alongside unit/host/package and rendered-layout gates. Workflow configuration is not evidence of a hosted CI pass; read the result at the actual pushed commit.

The unit matrix requires Ubuntu, Windows and macOS 26 on the standard Intel runner. Repeated hosted ARM capacity failures motivated the explicit Mac host selection; setup logs the OS and asserts actual Darwin/x64 execution. All tests and the native Windows prerequisite remain blocking. Passing Intel checks does not establish Apple Silicon host acceptance, which remains deferred capacity coverage.

docs.title: Model evaluation and limits
docs.text:
Eight reviewed conceptual topics are bundled with the API contracts. They cover sensitivity, classifier error costs, imbalance, held-out evaluation, prediction thresholds, nonlinear representation, learning rate and overfitting. Concept-only questions receive the relevant explanation without incidental API catalogues or fixture fallback; explicit code requests retain related reviewed contracts and complete linked examples, and exact API queries retain their contract precedence. Topic/source changes invalidate generated freshness. See Evaluation alignment for practical scaffolding, Run evidence, consent and current research procedures with their limits.

The Tutor should explain the requested concept first and use reference grounding quietly. Finding a fixture is not a learner achievement, and a default-only example does not establish that constructor options are unavailable. Reviewed contracts supply the complete positional forms. A decision-tree regression prompt preserves the reported Spanish question and checks the actual constructor options separately from the quality of a model's explanation.

kafe-vscode/test/evals/kafe-code.json contains general-language prompts and review criteria for real-provider evaluation. The generated library-api.json beside it adds bilingual coverage of every intended top-level library call, known limits, unknown APIs, execution boundaries and the reported decision-tree teaching regression. Repeat them when the language, model, teaching instructions, or retrieval changes. Include new capabilities and discovered mistakes. Compare answers against expected behavior, not only the presence of instruction text. Provider evaluations require a configured authorized provider; the deterministic tests do not contact DeepSeek.

Reference completeness means the intended shipped API has truthful contracts and evidence. It does not establish correctness of every model explanation, arbitrary architecture combination, learned model, proposed program or experimental backend path. Real-provider review should include English/Spanish API questions, exact member names, shape/precondition failures, unsupported bindings and requests with no executable runtime. Source provenance and zero exit are not correctness claims.

The Tutor should use show(...) for ordinary built-in output and explicitly invoke a driver function when a complete program defines one. Top-level snippets do not require a main wrapper. A user-defined print remains valid. Missing library documentation must remain an explicit uncertainty rather than a guessed API. Syntax parsing alone cannot prove those semantic or behavioral properties.

TeachingPolicy.js defines one guided baseline (kafe-guided-7) and independent guided/paused mode. Concept and syntax questions receive direct explanations; meaningful decisions invite one focused learner contribution without duplicate checkpoints. Bounded arithmetic and organization of supplied evidence are permitted while the learner retains the complete assessed submission and final individual conclusion. Feedback affirms supported reasoning and identifies at most one actual gap if present; a sound draft needs no forced revision. Aim for one manageable next step and at most one independent question when needed; there is no mandatory closing question or universal word cap. Brevity/detail requests affect presentation within eligible bounded history, not authority, accuracy or required reasoning. There is no durable style-memory field, Remember action, classifier or hidden preset. Compare actual provider responses against this common contract in English and Spanish; deterministic instruction checks do not establish provider compliance.

The development-only activity-dialogues.json adds two coherent Spanish rehearsals with three turns each: fraud comparison and XOR. Internal TP/FN and threshold oracles check synthetic mathematics, not teaching success. Integration tests use real composition/coordinator/history with a deterministic capturing provider, submit exact learner text and keep rubrics/oracles out of requests. Synthetic learner reports never become host Run or Apply evidence. The tests retain current-question reference selection and existing eligibility fences; they do not add history-based retrieval. Concept-only questions select the relevant concept without incidental API catalogues or fixture fallback; explicit code requests retain reviewed contracts and useful complete examples. The earlier four-message live pilot applies only to its retained sample.

Three subsequent six-turn actual-provider samples were independently reviewed and rejected: Flash at 156957e / guided-5 had arithmetic, XOR-count and unsupported evidence/domain claims; Flash at 39d43c5 / guided-6 reversed a false-negative/false-positive trade-off and drew XOR incorrectly; Pro at reviewed bytes later committed as bce92ee / guided-6 avoided those two errors but withheld bounded comparisons, manufactured a draft defect and made unsupported training/validation claims. Each round completed six requests and six replies with zero tools or transport failures. These are actual model replies to synthetic learner observations, not measured classifier results. Tokens and monetary cost were not measured.

After independently approved source clarification at e0794c1 / guided-7, the six-turn retest and two predefined held-out transfer/code checks completed eight requests/replies/settlements, with 3,009 contiguous sanitized diagnostic records, zero tools and zero failures. Independent review found a mixed result: the FN/FP comparison, XOR threshold count and affine upper bound were correct; held-out fraud sensitivity was correctly distinguished from accuracy, and bounded gesha.create_dense help matched the positional contract. However, X3 still invented training membership/settings and imposed an incorrect requirement for training/validation loss trends to assess overfitting. X2 overstated experimental isolation and repeated a settled baseline check; draft feedback retained an unnecessary missing-gap framing. The full answer-quality goal is not complete. Pro remains an experimental comparison default with thinking disabled and streaming enabled, without a model-winner or student-readiness claim. Those first four rounds used 26 actual provider requests; the earlier four-request pilot is separate. The failed and mixed samples remain evidence; no universal model ranking or novice-learning claim follows.

On 2026-10-28 the user chose Keep the current checkpoint. The Tutor guidance checkpoint remains at 9c25d04 / kafe-guided-7, deepseek-v4-pro, thinking disabled and streaming enabled. No further model calls, reasoning-mode experiment or protocol implementation is approved by that choice. The full answer-quality goal remains incomplete; retaining this checkpoint is not a model-winner, novice-readiness or classroom-efficacy verdict.

The final rehearsal on 9c25d04 completed the six canonical messages and one additional constructor request H3: seven requests/completions/completed settlements, 3,114 contiguous sanitized diagnostic records, zero tools and zero transport failures. Independent actual-answer review did not accept the sample. F1/F2 fraud interpretation and comparison were supported. X3 recalled the earlier 75% XOR baseline as about 50% and invented training membership and absent validation; X1 gave an unsupported cause for near-threshold scores, X2 overstated experimental isolation and F3 manufactured a conditional draft gap. H3 supplied valid machine.logistic_regression(0.1, 1000) and machine.gaussian_nb() creation fragments, with a minor inaccurate introductory claim about two forms for each model. Earlier H1/H2 remain round4-only evidence. Across five tuning rounds, 33 requests were made (6+6+6+8+7); the earlier four-request pilot is separate. Tokens and cost were not measured. These are real model answers to synthetic learner reports, not observed classifier results or novice outcomes.

At that checkpoint, read-only feasibility identified that a production-equivalent thinking-enabled comparison would need a new private reasoning/history, snapshot and parser contract. Production integration was deferred. A later approved tools-omitted follow-up is recorded below; the production reasoning-replay contract remains unimplemented.

Review actual responses for technical accuracy, direct explanation, a useful next step, reaction to learner reasoning, evidence origin and learner-owned choices. Record supported, concern or not observable with an exact excerpt and consequence; keep material failures visible. A first-semester support target is not an observed novice result. The proposal names later-semester groups and leaves its original fraud starter/data unnamed and absent. A separately attributed facilitator starter ZIP is prepared and independently reviewed; see classroom materials. Facilitator machine configuration and empirical novice completion/timing/learning outcomes remain separate gates; the completed source-specific native 1.96 gate is recorded below.

Task 9 Stage A at 9c25d04 passed 1,087 extension tests with one existing Windows symlink skip and zero failures, plus 134 focused composition/reference/evaluation checks, 211 native-fixture/host unit checks and 47 fresh affected Python reference/policy checks. All three reference freshness builders, syntax, spelling, authored policy and whitespace checks passed. Canonical prompts/oracles and assessment boundaries remain unchanged. Retained local full Python evidence remains 787 passes, four documented skips and 86.89% strict child-inclusive coverage with unchanged input proof; it is not a fresh full local run.

Historical native failures remain recorded: edbedc7 failed the trusted setup-result assertion; 507865d then passed 12/12 trusted cases but failed one of 12 untrusted cases on the Setup notification severity, leaving its final no-terminal assertion and packaging unreached. Task 9 corrected only the stale test expectation to the existing information-notification contract, preserving actual trust and denial guards.

Source 9c25d04 was pushed and its remote SHA independently verified. Its automatic Python workflow 40634874604 passed; extension workflow 40634874680 passed all three-platform units, layout and pinned-reference gates. Real Windows VS Code 1.96 job 122639811898 completed 12/12 trusted and 12/12 genuinely untrusted cases, including denied Run/Setup and the final no-KAFE-terminal assertion, then passed VSIX packaging and verification. Docs workflow 40634874746 validated successfully; deployment was skipped. Known DialogService headless trust-prompt stderr was retained without suppression or trust changes, so this is a completed native gate rather than a claim of pristine startup logs. These exact-revision CI receipts apply to source 9c25d04; later documentation-only commits require their own delivery receipts. The local 1.143.1 provider rehearsal remains separate from pinned 1.96 CI.

The single scoped correction re-review and original dcf1de2 package inspection are complete; the engineering checkpoint was approved with a minor recovery-ledger observation, distinct from incomplete answer-quality acceptance. Managed installation, physical IME/screen-reader speech, publication and empirical novice outcomes remain separate gates.

The final delivery also preserves the concurrently pushed Run-output work from 039fcea: unbuffered Python output, retained native terminal results and no Run entries in the rendered Tutor conversation. The Tutor policy, provider configuration and canonical rehearsal prompts remain unchanged. A fresh combined-tree aggregate passed 1,091 tests with one existing Windows skip and zero failures (1,092 total, 40.328 s); all 42 rendered browser cases passed (24.706 s). The earlier 9c25d04 native CI remains an exact-revision historical receipt; merged-source packaging and CI require their own receipts.

Response text is retained through accumulated streaming, ordinary completion and structured tool/checkpoint/proposal follow-ups. Completed display, history and export agree on that retained text. Semantic phrase matching no longer substitutes a whole answer. Safe Markdown, protocol validation, bounds and source guards still apply. A provider may display an unsupported mastery claim; the host never treats that prose as a learner score, permission or correctness verdict. Real-provider review must evaluate this accepted limitation; no extra repair-model request is made.

Suggested code remains a suggestion. Preparation, native Review, Apply, and learner-started Run retain separate permissions. A no-file proposal request receives an unavailable tool result and conversation can continue. A valid file target still requires current scope confirmation. Editing or removing a dependency invalidates a stale scope.

Reference completeness does not establish dependency security or managed-install acceptance. The dependency repair uses patched locked packages, retains mandatory audits and keeps the global seven-day uv waiting period with narrow security exceptions. Native host verification runs in GitHub CI when the pinned local host is unavailable. Report exact-revision workflow results separately from local checks. Existing published runtime assets remain unchanged; rebuilding or publishing an updated managed runtime is a separate release step. Real-provider evaluation and learning efficacy still require their own evidence.

docs.title: Stopped reasoning feasibility follow-up
docs.text:
On 28 October 2026, a later approved text-only reasoning feasibility follow-up produced 67 provider attempts: 63 completed replies and four initial 30-second timeouts. These are separate from the earlier 33 activity-tuning requests and the older four-request pilot. Existing blinded reviews found no clean accepted arm in the reviewed comparisons. The final 20-request cost-guidance ablation completed before the user stop was verified, but its answers remain unreviewed. No experimental policy or provider setting was adopted; production remains at the cad0bd1 implementation with kafe-guided-7, deepseek-v4-pro, thinking disabled and a 30-second timeout. Token usage and cost were not measured.

Separate feasibility block Attempts Completed Timeouts Answer review Initial 30-second fixed-prefix comparison 11 7 4 Incomplete comparison with concerns Separate 90-second fixed-prefix comparison 12 12 0 Neither arm accepted Separate 90-second own-history comparison 12 12 0 Neither arm accepted Current versus shorter instructions, both with reasoning 12 12 0 Neither variant accepted Final global cost-guidance ablation 20 20 0 Completed but unreviewed

The native test harness passed the existing saved key directly through VS Code SecretStorage to the original provider; the credential value was not inspected or extracted. Tools were omitted entirely, raw reasoning was discarded, and the receipts record no tool calls or native actions. Only literal synthetic learner questions and ordinary public reference context entered requests; offline oracles and review criteria stayed outside them. Both arms declared the full knowledge pack unavailable, with no included files or native evidence. These direct-provider tests do not establish compatibility with the normal tools-enabled extension.

The user approved a 90-second limit for the separate experiments; the normal 30-second timeout remains unchanged. Own-history comparisons used each arm's previous replies, so their later contexts differ. Fixed-prefix comparisons replayed earlier visible replies. The shorter contract and ablation were exploratory interventions with disclosed trade-offs, without demonstrated stable improvement. The four new cost cases were authored after the failure class was seen and are not pristine holdout evidence.

The user stopped the experiment and then authorized documentation, commits, pushing and CI repair until green. That delivery instruction does not resume provider calls, answer-quality review, tuning or adoption. Detailed experiment harnesses, transcripts and reviews remain local ignored artifacts. Further quality work requires explicit resumption.

The retained baseline receipt for cad0bd11 records successful Python tests, extension validation and documentation validation. CI establishes engineering gates for its exact revision; it does not validate Tutor answer quality or student readiness. Later documentation commits need their own observed checks.

docs.title: Rendered layout regression
docs.text:
The layout suite runs the shipped HTML, CSS, and browser scripts with synthetic conversation state. It checks document overflow, conversation reachability, fixed composer placement, and accessible speaker headings at narrow, short, and enlarged-text sizes.

Run npm run test:layout with an installed Playwright. KAFE_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE can name an existing installation and KAFE_LAYOUT_BROWSER an existing Chromium/Edge executable. The local test never downloads a browser. CI installs the pinned Playwright JavaScript tooling and uses the hosted Ubuntu image's preinstalled Chrome, logging its actual version. Missing Chrome fails setup; no layout assertion is skipped. This avoids apt/browser downloads that can exhaust the job before rendering begins. The browser version follows the runner image rather than a Playwright browser-build pin. This browser evidence is separate from native VS Code, physical IME, and screen-reader acceptance.

docs.title: Diagnosing a Tutor failure
docs.text:
After changing the development extension, restart its Extension Development Host or use Developer: Reload Window there. Reproduce the failed message once, then open View: Toggle Output and select KAFE Tutor Diagnostics. The channel is created when the first traced event occurs; it contains only fixed metadata categories and numbers. Messages, tool arguments, source text, paths, credentials, raw exception messages and stacks are excluded. The recent buffer is bounded to 256 records and clears with a trace-reset marker when full.

For a tool failure, inspect tool-start, tool-failed and turn-settled for the same local attempt number. reason distinguishes rejected arguments, invalid queries, missing captured sources and other validation categories. Known exception categories/codes are recorded; unclassified means the cause was not identified. turn-settled reports controller status and whether it remains busy. view-posted records VS Code's postMessage acceptance at a display revision; delivered: true does not prove the browser rendered it. The diagnostics never retry, resend or weaken a tool guard. They describe a reproduced attempt, not the cause of an older screenshot.

docs.title: Persistence, context and internal ownership
docs.text:
Archive payload v2 stores only mode at the historical kafeTutor.conversations.v1 key. Strict original v1 validation precedes transformation and full v2 validation. The original archive remains until successful serialized save; a failed write retains live retry/export recovery. After v2 save, v1-only readers are unsupported. No backup key or dual write exists; public export remains schema 1. Migration preserves content, identities, dates, selection and drafts, but cannot recover previously filtered-away model text.

The provider still receives at most eight eligible whole pairs / 32 KiB, while the full saved transcript remains readable/exportable. The context notice derives from the immutable captured submission's omissions, rather than a pre-send estimate; repeated identical conditions do not append transcript messages. Restoring clears optional source selections and executable authority. Source snapshots remain 64 KiB each, private Run output 1 MiB, and the archive retains its 200-chat / 10,000-entry / 5,000-pair / 4-MiB-content / 16-MiB-total limits. Export is independently bounded to 16 MiB. See the learner limits for other existing bounds.

Private mutation signatures trigger persistence bookkeeping; they are not authorization. Events share a detached, deeply frozen display projection; explicit snapshots/captures remain independently detached. Full persistence capture/normalization moves to debounced save and explicit list/export/switch/disposal boundaries, with complete store validation preserved. The controlled profile in the engineering benchmark records measures synchronous notifications and an in-memory storage adapter, not network latency, native rendering or real disk writes.

SessionCoordinator owns domain dependency enumeration and source/authorization revocation. The adapter retains native observation, real URI/filesystem authorization and freshness revisions, including rechecks after awaits. Its pure relevance query and source-change callback use the same native-active observation. The broader dependency union is metadata only: historical files do not gain admission or broaden ordinary edit relevance. ConversationSession.runTargetUris() reads the existing current-generation Run registry without creating another registry or restoring historical capabilities. Callback generation/disposal checks prevent an old event from mutating a newly selected conversation.

docs.title: Historical candidate evidence boundary (c944d88)
docs.text: This paragraph records the earlier candidate and its then-pending gates; current source receipts appear above. Final review correction c944d88 follows integration cleanup 524dac5 and packaging patch d074ff9. Nested revocation retains its original owner across display/proposal callbacks; original cancellation still settles and aborts when publication becomes stale. The final aggregate passes 1,032 extension tests with one existing Windows symlink-creation skip, all 42 browser cases, syntax, reference freshness and revised VSIX checks. Packaged guide links use the explicit reviewed b4d5371 documentation snapshot; the three guides and contributor-workflow anchor were checked in actual transformed package content. Remote publication/availability is separate. Development profiler, tests, credentials and runtime archives remain excluded. Nine unchanged Python inputs retain 787 passes, four documented skips and 86.89% strict child-inclusive coverage. Task11 dependency audits are retained with unchanged locks/configuration; no new audit query or timing claim is made. Initial whole-plan review requested the corrections; scoped final re-review and exact-revision hosted evidence remain pending. The exact native VS Code 1.96.0 executable/workbench are absent locally, so native host-policy and acceptance remain pending. The supported extension workflow can supply exact-revision hosted evidence after separately authorized push/dispatch; it does not substitute physical IME or screen-reader speech. Publication, managed-install acceptance, real-provider behavior and research outcomes remain separate gates.

docs.title: VS Code extension and AI Tutor
docs.text: Extension 2.4.1 provides KAFE highlighting, snippets, saved conversations and a unified Tutor in VS Code 1.96.0 or later. Runtime 0.5.0 uses a private, pinned CPython 3.11.15 environment that installs only the KAFE core; Hugging Face and Kaggle are optional packs installed on request. Package and dataset caches are reused across repairs. Reviewed MACHINE/GESHA guidance is bundled before runtime installation.

docs.title: Start chatting
docs.text:
1. Open KAFE: Open Tutor.
  2. Choose Configure Tutor if prompted, or KAFE: Configure Provider Key. Enter your DeepSeek API key in the masked native VS Code prompt; it stays in SecretStorage. Configuration records a stored key; it does not verify credentials. Configuration preserves your draft and never sends it.
  3. Type a concept or code question and choose Send. Ask for shorter or fuller explanations in the conversation when useful.

docs.title: Run your first saved program
docs.text:
1. Open a workspace folder and create or open a saved .kf file.
  2. In a trusted workspace, choose KAFE: Run File or Ctrl+F5 (Cmd+F5 on macOS).
  3. Read output, errors and interactive input in the native KAFE Run terminal. Run is separate from chat and applying a change.

Trusted activation automatically prepares a missing published runtime. Setup is noncancellable: hiding its progress is not cancellation. A failed setup offers a native retry and optional details; retry never sends your draft or runs a program. Chat with a configured provider and bundled references can work independently of Run setup.

docs.title: Your data and choices
docs.text:
Sending shares your message, eligible recent discussion and currently authorized context with DeepSeek. Optional files require explicit inclusion. Conversations and drafts are saved locally per workspace; exporting or sharing them is your choice and is not research consent. Restricted Mode supports message-only chat without file, edit or Run access. Credentials use native key entry, changes use native diffs, and execution uses native terminals.

See reliability, budgets and contributor checks and study procedures and consent for detail. Older package notes describe a historical candidate.

docs.title: Conversation
docs.text:
Type a message and press Send or Enter once. Shift+Enter inserts a newline. One answer streams in place. Stop replaces Send during a response while the next draft stays editable. Retry uses the original question and current authorized context, preserves the next draft and does not duplicate the learner message. Key configuration never sends automatically.

The included whole-file indicators identify the active eligible .kf and selected optional files. The file disclosure beside the composer lists visible same-workspace .kf metadata without reading optional contents; explicit inclusion permits capture at Send. Indicators reveal their named file natively; optional indicators can be removed. Accessible names and tooltips retain full identities, including duplicate basenames. Optional selection survives becoming active and closing its editors. Source/trust/knowledge changes fence admission and invalidate dependent authority. Restricted Mode permits message-only learning while excluding workspace files, edits and Run.

docs.title: Saved workspace conversations
docs.text:
The Tutor keeps multiple independent conversations in the current VS Code workspace. It saves their messages, drafts, completed history and guided/paused mode locally with a 250 ms debounce. Reopening the workspace restores the last selected chat. An empty untitled window uses its own VS Code workspace storage scope.

The view description shows the active title. Use its title actions or the Command Palette:

Command Behavior KAFE: New Conversation Saves the current chat and starts an empty guided conversation. KAFE: Switch Conversation Opens a native picker of saved chats with updated dates; restores the selected chat's draft and preferences. KAFE: Rename Conversation Renames the active chat. The initial automatic title comes from its first learner message. KAFE: Delete Conversation Requests confirmation before deleting the active chat and its draft; creates an empty chat if it was the last one. KAFE: Export Conversation Saves a snapshot of the selected chat through a native JSON Save dialog.

New, Switch and Delete stop an active provider response before transitioning and retain its partial text as cancelled. A current native Apply must finish before changing conversations. Switching clears selected optional sources, live learning decisions/observations, proposal/Run grants and private execution evidence. Stored checkpoint/proposal summaries remain readable without restoring their old native actions. An independently running program continues in its terminal; late results cannot populate another conversation.

docs.title: JSON export
docs.text:
Export produces one versioned UTF-8 JSON document containing the selected conversation's title, identity, creation/update dates, complete visible entries, statuses and safe display summaries. Text, code and Unicode are preserved exactly. The snapshot is captured before the Save dialog opens, so a later chat switch does not redirect the export. Cancelling the dialog writes nothing; a failed write reports an error and keeps the chat open. Export does not stop a response, so an unfinished reply can retain its responding status in the snapshot.

Drafts, learning preferences, provider history/dependencies, attached-source metadata and executable action handles are excluded from the public JSON. Text or code entered in the conversation remains part of its transcript. SecretStorage values, attached-file snapshots, raw provider requests and private Run evidence are never copied into it. JSON export has a separate 16 MiB bound and remains available for a live chat when archive saving fails, subject to that bound.

docs.title: Guided learning and permissions
docs.text:
One guided Tutor answers concept and syntax questions directly. At meaningful design choices it invites one focused hypothesis or decision, accepts reasoning already supplied and offers stronger hints or bounded examples when needed. Final comparisons, conclusions and assessed solutions remain the learner's work. KAFE: Pause/Resume Teaching independently removes or resumes additional reasoning requirements; changes during a response queue until settlement. The former Learning Level command and Beginner/Intermediate/Expert selector are retired, including their hidden presets.

Ask for brevity or detail in ordinary chat. This changes presentation within eligible conversation history; there is no Remember action, durable style memory or permanent style selector. Older messages can fall outside the provider context after omission, switching or restart.

A checkpoint identifies the Tutor's interpretation of a learner proposal. Confirm choice adopts the displayed approach without certifying authorship, understanding or correctness. Discuss and Skip give no preparation permission. Supporting evidence appears in labelled details; genuinely unresolved choices stay visible.

Prepare change authorizes one proposal for the exact displayed workspace-relative target and bounded scope. A missing key, failure or cancellation consumes that permission; a retry needs a fresh displayed scope. Native Review change, Apply, Dismiss, and explicit Run remain separate actions. Pure design confirmation never authorizes preparation.

docs.title: Credentials and native actions
docs.text:
Use KAFE: Configure Provider Key for the masked native DeepSeek input. The key stays in VS Code SecretStorage. Missing-key recovery preserves the draft; successful configuration never resends. KAFE: Clear Provider Key deletes that key from SecretStorage. Never put credentials in chat.

Review change opens the native diff. Apply requires reviewed current proposal identity and authorization of the target plus its complete dependencies, version and content hash. Source edits/deletion, revoked trust or reset invalidate stale proposals. Applying never runs the program. Provider tools cannot apply edits or execute programs.

Run main.kf identifies the saved-file target. KAFE: Run File and Ctrl+F5 (Cmd+F5 on macOS) require trust and a saved eligible file. Cancelled saving leaves it unrun. Input/output use the native terminal. Stop cancels the provider independently of Run; New conversation does not terminate an independently running process.

Run evidence distinguishes host-observed launch/completion/current saved-source comparisons from current editor comparisons. Missing comparisons and null exit outcomes remain unknown. Equal observed boundary hashes do not prove exact interpreter-read bytes, imported-file bytes or correctness. Zero exit is an exit result; Exact executed bytes: unknown and Correctness: not established remain explicit. Subsequent authorized explanations may use staged/applied/Run facts while retaining these limits.

docs.title: Retention and limits
docs.text:
Archive payload version 2 stores mode-only learning preferences at the existing kafeTutor.conversations.v1 storage key. Valid legacy v1 archives are strictly validated using their original rules before all former levels map to the common baseline. Loading leaves the original stored data untouched until a successful serialized v2 save. Older readers cannot read the archive after that save; downgrade is unsupported. Public JSON export remains schema version 1. Previously discarded response text cannot be recovered by migration.

The local workspace archive retains the full transcript, draft, completed history and learning preferences across restarts. It stores safe checkpoint/proposal summaries without restoring live decisions or executable authority. Source selections, request snapshots, pending proposals, transient observations/decisions and action/output evidence reset on transition or restart. Restored completed history keeps its original source/knowledge dependencies and must pass current context eligibility before use by the provider. Credentials and legacy progress remain independent. Legacy progress is neither imported into learning nor transmitted to the provider. KAFE: Clear Legacy Tutor Progress requests separate native confirmation and preserves saved/live chat and credentials.

The archive permits 200 conversations, 4 MiB per conversation and 16 MiB total, with at most 10,000 entries and 5,000 completed history pairs per conversation. Limits reject saving without silent eviction. Failed writes keep the current conversation live and display an error; retry or export before closing. Malformed existing storage is preserved instead of overwritten, and the warning identifies the current chat as temporary.

Follow-ups retain at most eight eligible completed whole learner/assistant pairs within 32 KiB UTF-8. Failed/interrupted pairs are excluded; removed or changed source/knowledge grounding omits dependent context without reviving it through learning records. Source snapshots are limited to 64 KiB each and Run output to 1 MiB. The five permitted tools retain four calls per response and four rounds per turn. Checkpoints are bounded to 16 KiB each; teaching retains at most 32 decisions, 32 observations and 64 KiB total state. Exhaustion rejects the admission without silently evicting pending records; New conversation clears this state. Host action evidence retains at most 32 whole records, 8 KiB each and 64 KiB total/projection text. Old discussion and adopted decisions are not current execution proof.

A short notice reports omissions in the actual submitted request, with optional details; it never resends or restores old file permission. The saved transcript and export include older visible messages beyond the eight-pair provider window. The private archive retains history dependency references but excludes attached source snapshots, SecretStorage values, raw provider requests, private Run evidence and raw transport errors. Visible message text/code and safe checkpoint summaries are retained. Tutor diagnostics continue to exclude transcript text and private content.

docs.title: Runtime and knowledge
docs.text:
The checksum-pinned KAFE 0.5.0 runtime archive ships inside the VSIX and is installed with uv 0.11.3. Setup verifies the bundled archive, downloads and verifies a private CPython 3.11.15, creates an isolated environment, and verifies that exact interpreter before marking the runtime ready. Repairs rebuild the environment while retaining the verified Python/package cache, and HF_HOME keeps downloaded Hugging Face data in KAFE's persistent data cache instead of downloading it again for each environment repair.

First setup installs only the KAFE core: private Python, uv and the ANTLR runtime. Programs that use import huggingface; or import kaggle; need an optional data pack. Run KAFE: Install Hugging Face Pack (Hugging Face datasets) or KAFE: Install Kaggle Pack (kagglehub, Pillow and py7zr) once, after the runtime is ready. Without the pack, those programs stop with a message that names the command. Packs are added without removing each other. A full runtime reinstall starts a fresh environment, so install the packs again; the package cache makes this fast. KafeHF and KafeKaggle import their packages only when a program calls them, so ordinary programs start quickly and do not initialize multiprocessing. multiprocess remains below 0.70.18 because newer releases call an unavailable private RLock method on affected Windows Python builds and print a shutdown traceback. Ordinary conversation with a configured provider can proceed without an executable runtime or knowledge pack; requests disclose unavailable knowledge. Invalid or changed knowledge is never represented as valid grounding.
